3 Background facts:
The victim (PW-1), on the date of the incident, was about 17 years old.
The informant (PW-2) is the mother of the victim.
The crime was initially registered on the basis of 213.apeal.98.2021.odt the report of the informant (PW-2) for the offence punishable under Section 363 of the IPC.
It is the case of the prosecution that on the date of the incident, the victim was studying in 12 th standard.
In the month of April 2015, at about 11:00 a.m., one unknown person had called on mobile phone of the mother of the victim.
The victim had attended the call.
On being asked by the caller, the victim disclosed her name.
The boy on the other side did not disclose his name.
It is stated that after this, on 2-3 occasions, the said boy made phone calls to the victim.
The victim black listed the said number.
The said boy again tried to contact the victim on phone.
He sent messages to the victim and requested her to attend his calls.
The said boy disclosed his name as Hemkrushna Meshram, resident of Sakoli.
The victim and the boy used to talk to each other and as a result thereof, the intimacy developed between them.
One day in April 2015, the accused told the victim to meet him.
He threatened her to kill her father if she did not meet him.
Due 213.apeal.98.2021.odt to this threat, the victim assured to meet him within 15 days.

4 As promised,
on 29.05.2015, at about 10:00 a.m. the victim went to Bhandara from Warthi.
From Bhandara she went to Sakoli and made a phone call to the accused.
The accused came there and identified her on the basis of the description provided by the victim to him.
The accused, at that time, disclosed his love for the victim.
The accused promised to marry her.
On that day, they were together for about an hour.
Thereafter, the victim returned to her village Warthi.
5 Thereafter, the accused visited the victim's house.
Her mother did not like his visit to their house.
Her father is blind.
On account of this visit of the accused to their house, the victim was sent to village Bela, District Bhandara at the house of her maternal aunt for two months.

In February 2016,
the victim had a practical examination and therefore, she Hemkrushna Gongal Sindhimeshram vs State Of Mah.

2 213.apeal.98.2021.odt returned to Warthi.
The accused again contacted her.
He called her at the railway station.
The victim went to the railway station.
They met there.
The accused again expressed his love and affection for the victim.
The victim refused to keep relations with him.
The accused threatened to commit suicide by leaving behind the suicide note, blaming her parents, in case she refused to perform marriage with him.

On 17.04.2016, there was a marriage in the house of Mr.
Bhujade at village Warthi.
At the request of the mother, the victim attended the said marriage.
The accused met her near the Ambedkar Statue.
The accused told her to bring her clothes and Adhar Card.
The victim followed his instructions.
They went to Nagpur railway station.

The accused,
thereafter, took her by bus to Secunderabad in Andhra Pradesh.
The accused took her in a hut near the building construction site.
The accused told the victim that he wanted to perform marriage with her.
The accused adorned her with Mangalsutra 213.apeal.98.2021.odt purchased from the market.

It is stated that the accused, thereafter,
committed sexual intercourse with the victim regularly.
One day the call made by the wife of the accused on his mobile phone was attended by the victim.
The victim made an inquiry with the lady on the other side.
The lady informed that she is the wife of the accused and they have two daughters.
On being questioned about it, in the evening, the accused admitted the same.

The victim, thereafter,
wanted to leave the said place, however, the accused beat her mercilessly under the influence of liquor.
The victim in the absence of the accused, made a phone call by using mobile phone of neighbour to her mother and informed her ordeal to her mother.
Mother, thereafter, went to the police station and informed about the call received from the victim from Secunderabad.
Police Officer PW-9 and neighbour PW-3 went to Secunderabad.
They took search of the victim.
They located the victim and the accused on 29.05.2016.
The victim narrated the entire 213.apeal.98.2021.odt incident to them.
PW-9 drew the spot panchanama as well as seizure panchanama on the spot.
They brought the accused and victim to Warthi.
On the basis of the statement of the victim, Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act were added in the crime.
The victim and accused were medically examined.
Their clothes were seized.
During the course of the investigation, the birth certificate of the victim was collected.
The statements of the witnesses were recorded.
After the completion of the investigation, the charge sheet was filed.
6 On committal of the case to the learned Special Judge by the Magistrate, the charge was framed against the accused.
The accused pleaded not guilty.
His defence is of a total denial.
7 In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined eleven witnesses.

The learned Judge,
213.apeal.98.2021.odt on consideration of the evidence, found the accused guilty of the offences punishable under Sections 363 and 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced him, as above.
The accused is, therefore, before this Court in appeal.
8 I have heard learned appointed Advocate Mr D. A. Sonawane for the appellant/accused and Ms S. V. Kolhe, learned APP for the State.
Perused the record and proceedings.
9 Learned Advocate for the appellant/accused submitted that the date of birth of the victim has not been proved beyond reasonable doubt.

sentences.text: Learned Advocate, therefore, submitted that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove that on the date of the commission of the offence the victim was below 18 years of age.
Learned Advocate submitted that the medical officer has not given a concrete opinion that 213.apeal.98.2021.odt the victim was subjected to sexual intercourse.
Learned Advocate took me through the evidence of medical officer PW-4 and the medical examination report at Exh. 23.
Learned Advocate submitted that the external injuries were not found on the person of the victim.
Learned Advocate submitted that only on the basis of the torn hymen the conclusion cannot be drawn that the victim was subjected to penetrative sexual assault in the recent past.
Learned Advocate submitted that the medical evidence is not sufficient to corroborate the oral evidence adduced by the prosecution.
Learned Advocate submitted that the version of the victim and her mother cannot be believed.
Learned Advocate submitted that victim, on her own, accompanied the accused.

Learned Advocate submitted that in the absence of concrete medical evidence, the oral evidence of the victim and her mother cannot be believed and relied upon to form the sole basis of conviction in such a serious offence.
Learned Advocate submitted that the conduct 213.apeal.98.2021.odt of the victim and her mother is unnatural and therefore, it creates doubt about very genesis of the case of the prosecution.
Learned Advocate submitted that the learned special Judge has failed to consider all the above stated facts and has come to the wrong conclusion.

10 Learned APP submitted that the evidence on record is sufficient to prove that the accused developed intimacy with the victim and on the false promise of marriage, kidnapped her from the custody of her lawful guardian.
Learned APP submitted that Exh. 14 is the birth certificate of the victim.

Learned APP submitted that the birth certificate has been proved by examining Village Development Officer and by production of the extract of the register, on the basis of which the certificate was issued.
Learned APP submitted that it has been proved beyond doubt that on the date of the offence the victim was under 18 years of age i.e. she was 17 years 5 months and 8 days old.

Learned APP submitted that,
213.apeal.98.2021.odt therefore, the defence of consensual sexual act by the accused with the victim is of no significance.

Learned APP submitted that the evidence on record is sufficient to prove that the victim, after kidnapping under the promise of marriage, was subjected to penetrative sexual assault by the accused for about one and a half months.
Learned APP submitted that the hymen of the victim was found to be torn at the time of the examination.
Learned APP submitted that the victim was taken into custody on 29.05.2016 and brought to Warthi by the police on 30.05.2016.

Learned APP submitted that this fact clearly suggests that during the stay of the accused and victim at Secunderabad, the accused, as stated by the victim, had committed the intercourse with her and therefore, the hymen was found to be torn.

Learned APP submitted that the question of external injury did not arise because the accused performed the intercourse under the promise of marriage and therefore, there was no question of resistance at the behest of 213.apeal.98.2021.odt the victim.
Learned APP submitted that the medical opinion was reserved by the doctor, subject to receipt of the report of the Analyst.

Learned APP submitted that merely because of the failure of the medical officer to give an opinion may not be vital to the case of the Hemkrushna Gongal Sindhimeshram vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Warthi Tah.Mohadi ... on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22398118/
4 prosecution because the examination of the private part of the victim clearly proves that she was subjected to sexual intercourse.

sentences.text: Learned APP submitted that the accused has not even suggested to the witness any reason for his false implication by the victim and her mother.
Learned APP submitted that in the ordinary course, such crimes are not reported on account of the stigmatic consequences of such reporting on the image of the family and the future of the victim.
Learned APP submitted that the learned Special Judge has properly appreciated the evidence.
Learned APP submitted that the evidence on record is sufficient to prove the charges against the accused.
11 In order to appreciate the rival submissions, I have 213.apeal.98.2021.odt gone through the record and proceeding.
At the outset, it would be necessary to consider the evidence with regard to the age of the victim.
The birth certificate of the victim was collected during the course of the investigation by the I.O.
It is at Exh. 14.
The birth certificate was issued by the Village Development Officer, Gram Panchayat, Warthi on 31.08.2009.

This certificate,
issued by the local authority, on the basis of the record maintained by the authority, has a presumptive value.
The prosecution, in order to set this controversy at rest, has examined Village Development Officer as PW-10.
PW-10 has produced a copy of the register where the entry of the birth date of the victim was taken.
It is at Exh.43.
PW-10 has deposed that the birth certificate at Exh. 14 was issued by Village Development Officer Mr Rautkar.
It is further seen that on the date of his evidence, he had brought the original birth register from the office.
The copy was compared with the birth register.
It is evident that in the 213.apeal.98.2021.odt extract of register, the birth entry is at serial number 135, whereas in the birth certificate the serial number of entry mentioned is 140.
In order to clear this ambiguity, the re- examination was conducted by the learned APP.
PW-10 has deposed in his evidence that all the entries in the original register were computerized and at that time, the defect in mentioning the serial number had crept in.
This evidence, in my view, is more than enough to prove the birth date of the victim.
On the basis of this evidence, it has been proved that the birth date of the victim is 09.11.1998.
The incident occurred on 17.04.2016.
It therefore goes without saying that the victim, on the date of the incident, was below 18 years of age.
I do not see any reason to discard or disbelieve this evidence.
The victim and her mother have deposed in unison about the birth date of the victim.

12 Before proceeding to consider the medical evidence, it is necessary to appreciate the evidence of the 213.apeal.98.2021.odt victim, her mother and other witnesses to find out whether the said evidence is sufficient to prove the charges against the accused.

It is not out of place to mention that since it has been proved that the victim was below 18 years of age on the date of the incident, even if the defence of the consent of the victim is accepted as it is, it would be of no help to take the case of the accused forward.
Since the victim has been proved to be below 18 years of age on the date of the incident, the act of accused will fall within the dragnet of the law.
13 PW-2 is the natural guardian of the victim.
The victim was taken out of custody without her consent.
The consent of the guardian was material and not that of the victim.
The victim was taken out of her guardianship without her consent and that too on a promise to marry by the accused.

5
There is ample evidence to prove that for about one and a half months, the victim and the accused stayed together at Secunderabad.

The evidence of PW-2, PW-3 and police 213.apeal.98.2021.odt Officer ASI PW-9 is sufficient to prove that on receipt of the information as to the whereabouts of the victim, they had gone to the Secunderabad and they found the accused and the victim residing together in a room.
This oral evidence has been corroborated by contemporaneous documentary evidence.
There is documentary evidence to prove that PW-9, upon receipt of the phone call from the victim by her mother, was deputed to Secunderabad to carry out the necessary investigation.

The written order given to PW-9 by the Assistant Police Inspector,
Warthi to that effect is at Exh. 34.
Exh. 37 is a letter given by PW-9 to the PSO Ghotke Sir, PS Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, whereby the request was made to provide them with the necessary help for arresting the accused.
Exh. 38 is the report made by PW-9 to the incharge of PS Warthi after coming back from Secunderabad.
Exh. 39 is the certified extract of the station diary entries.
These contemporaneous documentary evidence corroborates the 213.apeal.98.2021.odt version of PW-1, 2 and 3.
They have deposed that the victim was found in the custody of the accused.
The police arrested the accused and brought the victim and accused to village Warthi.
In my view, this evidence is sufficient to prove beyond doubt the offence of kidnapping.
Learned Special Judge has properly appreciated this evidence.
The finding recorded on this point is therefore unassailable.
14 The next important aspect is whether the victim was subjected to sexual intercourse by the accused, as stated by the victim.
For this purpose, it would be necessary to minutely peruse the evidence of the victim.
As far as the intercourse is concerned, the victim is the only witness to vouch about it.
The victim on the date of the incident was 17 years 5 months and 8 days old.
Her evidence is required to be appreciated with great care and caution.
It is a settled position in law that the sole testimony of the victim of a stellar quality can be made the basis of the conviction for the offence of rape.
It needs to 213.apeal.98.2021.odt be stated at this stage that in such a crime, rarely there will be a wild statement or overstating of the case by a girl or women to falsely implicate the accused.
The victim on the date of the incident was unmarried.
The unmarried women would apprehend, that the reporting of such a matter would make it difficult for her to secure an alliance with a suitable match from a respectable or acceptable family.
Such offence involves a fear of being taunted by others.
The offence involves extreme embarrassment.
In such a crime the natural inclination would be to avoid giving publicity to such incident, lest the family name and family honour is brought into controversy.

The parents of unmarried girl as also the husband and members of the husband's family of a married woman, in such a crime, would also more often want to avoid publicity on account of fear of social stigma on the family name and family honour.
In my view, the above factors would be very relevant while appreciating the defence of false implication raised by 213.apeal.98.2021.odt the accused.

The victim is the only daughter of the couple.
Her father is blind.
Her mother is the sole earning member of the family.
The victim was studying at the time of the incident.
The accused, who is a resident of Gondia, the adjoining district of Bhandara, was not known to the victim.
He established contact with the victim on telephone.
He extended threats to the victim of dire consequences, if she refused to establish relations with him.
The victim girl, in her deposition, has narrated a first hand account of the incident.
In her evidence, she has narrated in detail how the intimacy was developed between them and how ultimately it resulted in a kidnapping from the guardianship of her mother.
She has categorically stated that the accused had promised to marry with her and on the false promise to marry, took her to Secunderabad and there sexually abused her for one and a half months.

She has stated that one day she came to know, on receipt of a phone call from 213.apeal.98.2021.odt the lady whose identity was latter established to be the wife of the accused,
that the accused was married and having two daughters.

The accused, as stated by the victim,
admitted this fact.
She has stated that after this, she was not willing to stay with the accused.
But the accused was not ready to leave her.
He tortured her under the influence of liquor.
She has stated that somehow she managed to make a phone call to her mother and narrated the incident to her.
The mother had already lodged the missing complaint of the victim.
On receipt of this call from the victim, the mother went to the police station and narrated this fact to the police.
It is true that the report is silent about the name of the said person as well as his phone number.
However, this aspect has also been corroborated by contemporaneous documentary evidence.

The said documentary evidence is the station diary entry made at Warthi police station, when the mother of the victim reported this fact to the police and also the order at Exh. 34, issued by 213.apeal.98.2021.odt the API, Warthi to PW-9 to proceed to Secunderabad for this purpose.
There is a specific mention in the written order at Exh. 34 that the mother of the victim received a phone call from victim and on the phone, the victim disclosed her whereabouts to the mother.

The evidence of the victim, the evidence of PW-2, the mother of the victim, the evidence of PW-3, the neighbour who had accompanied them to Secunderabad and the evidence of PW-9, the police officer are consistent on this aspect.
This evidence corroborates the version of the victim that she was taken to Secunderabad by the accused and she was kept in one room nearby the construction site.
16 I have perused the cross-examination of the victim.
Perusal of the cross-examination would show that the core and crux of her deposition as to the kidnapping and penetrative sexual assault on her by the accused have not been shaken at all.

If the above stated factors, which are commonly prevalent in 213.apeal.98.2021.odt our society, are considered in juxtaposition with the defence of the accused, it would be highly impossible to conclude that on same trivial reason a girl studying in 12 th standard,
would spoil her entire future life.
Same would be equally applicable in case of the informant as well.
The accused has not placed on record any reason for his false implication.
There was no reason as such for PW-1 and her mother to falsely implicate the accused.
The missing report lodged by the mother is the most important document to prove that the victim went missing from 17.04.2016 and she was traced out on 29.05.2016.
As far as the oral evidence of the victim is concerned, I do not see any reason to discard or disbelieve the same.

sentences.text: The evidence of PW-1 has been corroborated by the evidence of her mother.
The mother has narrated that once or twice the accused came to their house.
She had scolded the accused.
PW-2 has narrated that her daughter told her that 213.apeal.98.2021.odt the accused had sexually abused her.
PW-2 as well as PW-9 have deposed that when they apprehended the accused and victim, the victim told them that the accused committed sexual intercourse with her.
Their visit to Secunderabad has been corroborated by documentary evidence.
The accused and the victim stayed together in the said room for about one and a half months.
Therefore, this statement of the victim that during this period she was subjected to sexual intercourse by the accused cannot be disbelieved.
The evidence is concrete and cogent.
18 It would be necessary to appreciate the medical evidence.
The victim was brought back to Warthi on 30.05.2016.
She was sent to the Civil Hospital, Bhandara, for a medical examination.
At the time of her examination, she narrated the history of assault to the medical officer.
She told the medical officer that she was kidnapped by the accused and subjected to sexual intercourse by the accused.
On 213.apeal.98.2021.odt examination by the medical officer, she found that on that day victim had a menstruation cycle.
There was bleeding.
On examination of the private part, the medical officer found that her hymen was torn.
The medical officer did not give any opinion on that day.
The medical officer reserved her final opinion, subject to the receipt of the report of the chemical analyzer.
As far as the report of CA is concerned, the report is not positive.
It needs to be stated that it was not expected to get a positive report as to the presence of the blood or semen stains of the accused on her clothes.
It is true that the hymen tear is possible while cycling or on account of sustaining any injury to private part.
It is nobody's case that the victim had a chance to do all these acts in between.
The medical evidence, therefore, corroborates the version of the victim that she was subjected to sexual intercourse.
The victim on the date of the incident was 17 years 5 months and 8 days old.
Considering her mature age, other injuries to her private part may not be 213.apeal.98.2021.odt possible.
In the facts and circumstances, I conclude that the learned Judge was right in holding that the medical certificate is the most important corroborative piece of evidence.
19 The accused has invited further trouble.
The photographs were produced on record by the accused.
Photographs are collectively marked as Exh. 53.
In the photographs, the accused and victim are seen together.
The accused has admitted these photographs.
Mangalsutra tied by the accused was seized.
It is at Article A.
The accused, in order to show that the victim was residing with her as his wife, took this precaution.
He promised her to marry but did not marry her.

When the victim came to know that he was married and had two daughters, she questioned him and therefore,
the real dispute between them started.
It is evident that by that time, much water had already flown under the bridge.
The accused, by his acts, had invited serious trouble under the law.
The knowledge of the accused as to the age of the victim is 213.apeal.98.2021.odt immaterial.
What is material is the actual age of the victim.
The victim on the date of the incident was below 18 years of age.
In my view, therefore, in this case, charges have been proved.
Learned Judge was right in holding the accused guilty and awarding him the sentence.
